findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: flow.py:1645-1650 records and commits, then moves the ref to `landed`; driven on a feature branch, solo and `develop`: main == HEAD == chore: land T-1
findings.message: `land` moves the mainline to HEAD and only then commits the merged bookkeeping on the current branch, so the mainline never carries the record it just wrote (driven: `main` = the task commit, `feature` = task + `chore: land`). On `main`, `next` says land again, `land` writes a second divergent `chore: land T-1`, and the next land from the feature branch is refused with `main has commits HEAD does not`.
findings.minimal_fix: mark merged and commit first, then `git branch -f <default> HEAD`; update the assertion at tests/test_aegis.py:1085

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: flow.py:1636-1643 refuses on git worktree list before _set_status; driven with main in a second worktree: exit 2, status gated, tree clean
findings.message: `land` marks the tasks merged and commits before `git branch -f`, so when git refuses the move — the mainline checked out in another worktree — the record says merged and the mainline never carries the work. Afterwards `land` says `nothing to land`, `next` says plan the next feature, and no `aegis` command recovers it.
findings.minimal_fix: before `_set_status`, refuse when `git worktree list --porcelain` lists `branch refs/heads/<default>` at another path

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: skills/build/SKILL.md:124 and .aegis/protocols/build.md:124 end at `ideally a different model.`
findings.message: `tier A needs the minimum number of review rounds `aegis lens plan` prints, even when the first is clean` — the plan no longer prints one and the gate no longer enforces one, so the orchestrator dispatches a second lens round for nothing; it also contradicts the one-rule paragraph fifteen lines above.
findings.minimal_fix: delete the clause after `different model`; re-vendor the protocol

findings.message: Holding is listed as `building`, `review`, `refine`, `docs`, `gated`; the three middle statuses were deleted (`HOLDING = ("building", "gated")`). This is the one ordered list R-28 says a reader answers ownership from.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 3: flow.py:1753-1755 wraps check_docs in apply_waivers; driven with a valid docs waiver and a current receipt, next says aegis land
findings.message: The docs step reads `check_docs` without `apply_waivers` while the merge gate applies them, so with a `docs` waiver `next` says `write the documentation` on every run while `aegis land` passes. `next --run` never reaches land.

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: flow.py:1746 runs `check_docs(closing_feature=True)` over each gated task before the land step
findings.message: The docs step and the `merge the branch` step are unreachable in the ordinary flow: a gated task with a clean tree always satisfies `_land_pending`, so the land step fires first. With the profile's diagram missing, `next` repeats `land the branch` for ever and only `land`'s stderr names the cause, which is the hole R-31 described.
findings.minimal_fix: run `check_docs(scope, closing_feature=True)` over the gated tasks before advising land, or delete the two dead steps

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: README.md:85-86 names the task gate, the merge gate and `aegis land`
findings.message: `aegis next --run` executes every `cli` step, and `aegis land` and `aegis gate --stage merge` are `cli` — so `--run` moves the mainline ref and commits. The sentence says it runs the task gate `and nothing else`.
findings.minimal_fix: name the three: the task gate, the merge gate, and `land`

findings.disposition_reason: lens-correctness round 2: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:257-259: the tier decides the independent reviewer; a second round for the count is not required
findings.message: §4 says the tier decides a minimum number of review rounds that `aegis lens plan` prints and `check_reviews` enforces; `min_review_rounds` was deleted from both and nothing reads the tier's `review_rounds`. A reader plans an extra round the gate does not require.
findings.minimal_fix: cut the minimum-rounds clause; keep the independent-reviewer sentence
